rv.q: Darkling is a worthy reminder of an often-overlooked disaster – but one that may well fail to take root in the mind.
A harrowing and intriguing account of a young woman’s struggles in the face of much adversity.
Frustrated by stunted writing, Darkling doesn’t penetrate beyond the surface level of its ideas.
But it’s the overall tone that is difficult.
The emotion captured through the design elements of this production is simply incredible.

While it takes too long to get to the essence of the play, and then draws out its conclusion, Darkling is still a story told with the necessary heaviness and severity, as well as rightful fury at the lack of justice afforded to the victims.

cn.t: Berthelsen delivers a powerful performance in this poetic monologue about the 1984 Bhopal disaster, but critics remain divided on whether Halder's lyrical script fully captures the catastrophe's horror and scale.
